mentions.name: Cangjie Workbook
mentions.description: This web application teaches the Cangjie input method (倉頡輸法), a visual way of decomposing Chinese characters, using a teaching approach inspired by how QWERTY is taught. It includes texts, lessons, and per-character annotations showing how characters are composed; the demo version requires no login.
mentions.problem: The Cangjie input method has a high initial learning curve.
mentions.source_excerpt: I've been working on a web application for learning 倉頡輸法 https://demo.cangjieworkbook.com/ , no login required for the demo version (Cangjie Input method). It's a visual way of decomposing Chinese characters.

mentions.name: Cangjie Workbook practice app
mentions.description: This app teaches Cangjie, a Chinese input method based on a visual decomposition of characters in which each character is represented by one to five codes. It teaches the method the way keyboarding (QWERTY) is taught to young students: first learning the location of the keys, then basic words, then typing sentences. A free demo is available.
mentions.source_excerpt: The second thing I am working on is an application to practice Cangjie. It's a Chinese input method that has been around for a long time. It is based on a visual decomposition of characters. Each character is represented by one to five codes and the majority are unique. My application teaches Cangjie like keyboarding (QWERTY) is taught to young students.
